chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man bequeathed to his children, and among them were adults who had attained maturity, and among them were young ones. Is it permissible for the adults to execute his bequest and pay his debt, for whom the debt was established upon the deceased with just witnesses, before the young heirs reach maturity? So he (peace be upon him) signed: Yes, it is upon the adults from the children to pay their father's debt, and not to detain him because of that.
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the deceased's debts when there are both adult and minor heirs?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) confirms that adult heirs bear the primary responsibility for settling the deceased's debts using the estate's assets, ensuring that the process is not delayed until the minors reach maturity. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that debt repayment is a priority claim on the estate, distinct from the inheritance distribution, thereby protecting the financial rights of creditors before the division of remaining assets among all heirs.

en.hubeali: ‘Muhammad Bin Al-Hassan wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man bequeathed to his children, and among them were adults who had attained puberty, and among them were young ones. Is it allowed for the adults that they can enforce his bequest, and pay-off his debts for the one who is correct upon the deceased with just witnesses before the young ones mature?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> signed: ‘Yes. It is upon the adults from the children that they pay-off debts, and not let him be imprisoned by that (debts)’.
en.sarwar: Once Muhammad ibn al-Hassan wrote to abu Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who made a bequest for his children consisting of adults and minor ones, if it is lawful for the adults to execute the will, pay off his debts to the rightful creditors according to just witnesses before the minors become adults. He (the Imam) signed the answer that said, ‘The adult children must pay the debts of their father and they must not allow him to remain imprisoned thereby (the debts).”’
